clue.text: These cops to turn out with means of detecting trouble inside

indicators.note: to turn out is to come out differently, so the letters of these, cops and to are rearranged

explanation.surface: Police officers are told to turn out armed with a way of spotting trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like a link word but is part of the anagram pool; 'turn out' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's listening device detects heart and chest problems inside the body.

clue.text: Band together?

parts.note: read as a musical direction: the whole band or orchestra playing at once, a score marking in Italian

explanation.walkthrough: 'Band together' looks like a verb, to unite; it is the instruction in a score for all the players to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this Italian term marks a passage played by all performers at once.

clue.text: Call it the last white-ant

parts.note: to term something is to call or name it

indicators.note: the last means only the final letter of the word the is taken

explanation.surface: Someone names an insect as the final white ant.
explanation.definitionFit: The so-called white ant is a wood-eating insect, not truly an ant at all.

clue.text: Native, for example, found in bed

definitions.text: Native, for example, found in bed

parts.words: Native, for example, found in bed
parts.note: a native is a British cultivated shellfish variety, and such shellfish grow in beds on the sea floor

explanation.walkthrough: 'Native' suggests a local person and 'bed' a bedroom; both belong to shellfish farming instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives are prized Whitstable-type bivalves, and they are raised on beds in estuaries.

clue.text: Treble heard in the stalls

parts.note: a treble here is a high young singing voice, and the stalls are the choir stalls of a church

explanation.walkthrough: 'stalls' suggests theatre seats, but it means the seating for singers in a church chancel.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy soprano sings the treble part from the chancel stalls.

clue.text: Carry the day, having half of previous trouble

indicators.note: half of the eight-letter word previous means its first four letters

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Someone wins through despite half of an earlier problem.
explanation.definitionFit: To win or triumph is to carry the day.

clue.text: Latin speech is excited where Michelangelo's work is seen

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of Latin speech is are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An animated sermon in Latin is delivered where the great painter's frescoes look down.
explanation.walkthrough: The page as scanned shows 'word', a misread of 'work': the Vatican chapel holds Michelangelo's ceiling frescoes.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal chapel in the Vatican has Michelangelo's painted ceiling and Last Judgement.

clue.text: After tin, tries out box for holding tea

indicators.note: after says the next piece follows the word for tin

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: out here means wrongly arranged, so the letters of tries are mixed up

explanation.surface: Having tried the tin, someone tries out a tea caddy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea caddy is a small lidded container for keeping tea leaves.

clue.text: It has our things in it (the blackest, so it turns out)

definitions.text: It has our things in it

indicators.note: turns out means comes out differently, so the letters of the blackest so are rearranged

explanation.surface: A container's contents prove to be the darkest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' before 'turns out' is a link word; the anagram pool is the three words in the brackets before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundry hamper holds our garments waiting to be washed.

clue.text: Nitre compound in Bury

indicators.note: compound means mixed together, so the letters of nitre are rearranged

explanation.surface: Saltpetre is used as a compound in a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the Lancashire town; it is the verb to put in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to lay a body in a grave, which is to bury it.

clue.text: No prison-maker in general?

parts.note: recalls Lovelace's line that walls of rock do not make a prison, and a Confederate general nicknamed for standing firm

explanation.walkthrough: Lovelace wrote 'Stone walls do not a prison make'; Thomas Jackson, the American Civil War general, was nicknamed for standing like such a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackson the Confederate commander earned this nickname, and the poem says such walls make no prison.

clue.text: Descriptive ofthe heaviest whip in the house

definitions.text: Descriptive ofthe heaviest whip in the house

parts.words: Descriptive ofthe heaviest whip in the house
parts.note: a three-line whip is the strictest voting instruction a party gives its MPs in the House of Commons

explanation.walkthrough: A whip in Parliament is an order to vote, underlined once, twice or three times by urgency; the heaviest has three lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means having three lines, as the strongest parliamentary whip is underlined thrice.

clue.text: Inclined to get a jousting contest

parts.note: a tilt is a joust between knights on horseback

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to take part in a tournament joust.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tipped at an angle is tilted or sloping.

clue.text: Such tenders leave room for improvement at the end of the day

definitions.text: Such tenders leave room for improvement at the end of the day

parts.words: Such tenders leave room for improvement at the end of the day
parts.note: tenders are carers of the sick, who go off shift leaving a ward of patients getting better

explanation.walkthrough: 'leave room for improvement' sounds like faint criticism; literally, carers leave a sickroom where patients are recovering.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital carers tend patients, then leave the ward when their shift ends.

clue.text: Reg at no time returning to be a retaliator

indicators.note: returning means the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: Reg is a man's name, taken as written
at no time means never

explanation.surface: A man called Reg never goes back to take vengeance.
explanation.definitionFit: One who takes vengeance is a retaliator, as in Jacobean revenge tragedy.

clue.text: Game in which the ball is always dropped

definitions.text: Game in which the ball is always dropped

parts.words: Game in which the ball is always dropped
parts.note: in this casino wheel game the croupier drops a small ball onto the spinning wheel every time

explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' suggests a fumble in a ball game; in this casino game dropping the ball is how every spin begins.
explanation.definitionFit: The casino wheel game starts each spin by releasing a ball onto the turning wheel.

clue.text: Loud pair of drawers featured in it.

definitions.text: Loud pair of drawers featured in it.

parts.words: Loud pair of drawers featured in it.
parts.note: drawers here are people who draw pistols, and a duel between two of them is noisy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Loud pair of drawers' suggests garish underwear; drawers are gunslingers drawing their weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wild West shoot-out is a noisy duel between two people drawing pistols.

clue.text: Longing for Jones's wife?

parts.note: the commandment forbids desiring your neighbour's wife, and the Joneses are the proverbial neighbours

explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping up with the Joneses' makes the Joneses the typical neighbours; the Tenth Commandment says not to desire a neighbour's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiring what belongs to another, such as a neighbour's spouse, is greedy envy.

clue.text: Scots not involved in such prices?

definitions.text: Scots not involved in such prices?

parts.words: Scots not involved in such prices?
parts.note: scot is an old word for a levy or tax, so prices without scots include no duty

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scots' suggests people from Scotland; scot is an archaic word for a tax, as in 'scot-free'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices with no duty or levy added are exempt from duty.

clue.text: Hamlet's specific difficulty

parts.note: recalls the 'To be or not to be' soliloquy, where the prince names his particular obstacle

explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet's soliloquy: 'To sleep, perchance to dream: ay, there's the rub'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's prince calls the precise snag, fear of dreams after death, by this phrase.

clue.text: R. Thames variety of rodent

indicators.note: a variety of means a different form of, so the letters of R Thames are rearranged

explanation.surface: Along the River Thames lives a kind of rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: A small burrowing creature kept as a pet is a kind of rodent.

clue.text: Indian girls' dance naturally short, to include what is socially acceptable

indicators.note: to include means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: natch is a slangy shortening of naturally
U means upper-class and so socially acceptable, from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U

explanation.surface: An Indian dance comes naturally, briefly, with polite manners included.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were labels for upper-class and not upper-class English usage.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional performance by professional dancing girls in India.

clue.text: Pinch, for example, can make girl cross

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A pinch can make a girl angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry; it is the letter shaped like a cross. 'Pinch' is not a nip but to take.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch something is to take it for yourself, as a state seizes territory.

clue.text: Men's graft produces these scraps

indicators.note: produces means makes something new, so the letters of men's graft are reworked

explanation.surface: Men's hard work yields only bits and pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'graft' is British slang for hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken bits or leftovers are small pieces.

clue.text: Wimbledon umpire's call while still in bed

definitions.meaning: a tennis umpire calls this when a player reaches the ball only after its second bounce
someone who has not yet risen in the morning

explanation.definitionFit: The tennis call means the ball bounced twice; said of a sleeper it means not yet risen.

clue.text: Observe first at Bath having girth adjusted? It is a plant!

parts.note: to eye something is to observe it

indicators.note: first at means only the opening letter of Bath is taken
adjusted means altered, so the letters of girth are rearranged

explanation.surface: At Bath someone first watches a horse's saddle strap being tightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girth' is a saddle strap; Bath is an English spa city.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphrasia is a small wild flower once used to treat sore eyes.

clue.text: It retires before the tenth

indicators.note: before means this piece comes ahead of the next
retires means goes back, so the word it is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws ahead of the tenth item.
explanation.definitionFit: A church levy was traditionally one tenth of produce or income.

clue.text: Pay the earth, perhaps, for arthritis treatment?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a different version, so the letters of pay the earth are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is it worth paying a fortune for relief of aching joints?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pay the earth' looks like the idiom for paying a fortune; it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying warmth to stiff joints is a common remedy for joint pain.
